items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to continuing the New York
State Smart Scholars Early College High School Program and the New York State
Pathways in Technology Early College High School Program in this state
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7464

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to continuing the New
York State Smart Scholars Early College High School Program and the New
York State Pathways in Technology Early College High School Program in
this state

 
PURPOSE OF THE BILL:

To preserve and continue the New York State Smart Scholars early college
high school (NYS Smart Scholars ECHS) program and the New York State
pathways in technology early college high school (NYS P-TECH) program in
this state, which provides various students, including those tradi-
tionally underrepresented in post-secondary education, with the opportu-
nity to access college-level courses, college degree credits, and career
preparation credentials through college-level programs at the high
school level with the combined support of high school and college staff
and resources, and for the NYS P-TECH programs, career training and
employment in a highly skilled job upon completion of the program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill establishes the legislative intent of the bill.

Section 2 of the bill adds a new Education Law § 6457 to establish grant
awards for NYS Smart Scholars ECHS programs. Subject to an appropri-
ation, the bill requires the Commissioner to first make funding avail-
able for previously funded NYS Smart Scholars ECHS programs that meet
the requirements of the new section and any remaining funds shall be
made available for new programs approved by the Commissioner in accord-
ance with the Commissioner's regulations.  The bill requires the Commis-
sioner to prioritize eligible applicants that demonstrate the willing-
ness and capacity to serve students who have been identified as
economically disadvantaged and/or academically at-risk for not success-
fully completing high school or not enrolling in or succeeding in
college.

The bill provides that, notwithstanding any other provision of the law
to the contrary, previously approved NYS Smart Scholars ECHS programs
that were funded under a prior request for proposals process and whose
contracts have been continuously renewed by the Department shall not
have to compete for funding under this section; provided that such
program meets certain benchmarks and program requirements as prescribed
by the Department in order to demonstrate that it continues to be a
successful NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program. If the program fails to meet
certain benchmarks and program requirements, it may be subject to
certain corrective action as described in the Commissioner's regulations
which may include but not be limited to establishing timelines to meet
program standards, a limitation on enrollment, termination of the
contract and/or grant, closure of the program and/or requiring a teach-
out agreement with an approved NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program to
describe how students will be transferred to such programs upon closure.
Any NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program approved pursuant to a prior request
for proposal process shall not be required to reapply for funds under
this section unless they are offering a new NYS Smart Scholars ECHS
program as determined by the Commissioner. Eligible institutions shall
file an application for approval by the Commissioner in a timeframe and
manner prescribed by the Commissioner in regulations, and, subject to an
appropriation, the Commissioner shall make awards to eligible applicants
for new Smart Scholars ECHS programs through a request for proposals
process.

This section of the bill defines an eligible applicant as a New York
State school district, a board of cooperative educational services
(BOCES), or a not-for-profit institution of higher education, in a part-
nership for the purpose of offering a NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program to
eligible students, any of which may serve as the fiscal agent. It
further defines an eligible student as a student who is a resident of a
partnering school district, or a resident of a component district of a
partnering BOCES and is enrolled in such district. School districts that
offer Smart Scholars ECHS programs under this section shall provide all
students with disabilities and English language learners enrolled in
such program with any support services and programs required under
federal and/or State law or regulations.

The bill also requires that monies made available under this section can
only be spent for the following purposes: to provide additional staffing
for the NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program, including a program director
and college liaison; student recruitment activities; to provide profes-
sional development to promote the NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program,
including cross-curriculum development between secondary and post-secon-
dary education partners to ensure curriculum alignment that prepares
students to succeed in college level courses while in high school; work-
shops and planning meetings between partners, including counselors,
parents, and college faculty, to support program sustainability and
build awareness in the regions on the benefits of having such programs;
academic and social support services to promote college readiness and a
college-going culture; transportation for students to take courses and
participate in activities at the NYS Smart Scholars ECHS site and at the
partner campus of the higher education partner; and tuition, books and
fees; provided however that tuition reimbursement shall only be allow-
able for non-remedial, credit-bearing college courses. Monies may also
be spent to implement any corrective action plan issued under this
section and/or for tuition, books and fees for non-remedial, credit-
bearing college courses at an institution of higher education for
students who were enrolled in a NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program that
subsequently closes before the student completes the program; provided
such student is taking comparable courses to what was offered in the
Smart Scholars ECHS program as determined by the Commissioner.

The bill further provides that no funds awarded under this section shall
be made available to support the regular academic program of any school
district or institution participating in this program.

Section 2 of the bill adds a new Education Law § 6458 to establish grant
awards for NYS P-TECH programs. Subject to an appropriation, the bill
requires the Commissioner to allocate funds first to previously funded
NYS P-TECH programs that meet the requirements of this section and any
remaining funds shall be available for new P-TECH programs approved by
the commissioner in accordance with the Commissioner's regulations. The
bill requires the Commissioner to prioritize eligible applicants that
demonstrate the willingness and capacity to serve students who have been
identified as economically disadvantaged and/or academically at-risk for

not successfully completing high school or not enrolling in or succeed-
ing in college.

The bill also provides that, notwithstanding any other provision of law
to the contrary, previously approved NYS P-TECH programs that were fund-
ed under a prior request for proposals process and whose contracts have
been continuously renewed by the Department shall not have to compete
for funding under this section; provided that such program meets certain
benchmarks and program requirements as prescribed by the Department in
order to demonstrate that it continues to be a successful NYS P-TECH
program. If the program fails to meet certain benchmarks and program
requirements, it may be subject to certain corrective action as
described in the Commissioner's regulations which may include but not be
limited to establishing timelines to meet program standards, a limita-
tion on enrollment, termination of the contract and/or grant, closure of
the program and/or requiring a teach-out agreement with an approved NYS
P-TECH program to describe how students will be transferred to such
programs upon closure. Any NYS P-TECH program approved pursuant to a
prior request for proposals process shall not be required to reapply for
funds under this section unless they are offering a new NYS P-TECH
program as determined by the Commissioner. Eligible institutions shall
file an application for approval by the Commissioner in a timeframe and
manner prescribed by the Commissioner in regulations, and, subject to an
appropriation, the Commissioner shall make awards to eligible applicants
for new P-TECH programs through a request for proposals process.

This section defines an eligible applicant as a New York State school
district or BOCES, either of which may serve as the fiscal agent. An
eligible district may work in cooperation with other school districts, a
BOCES, or any combination of these entities as a consortium applicant,
with a partnership that includes: (i) one or more New York State public
or not-for-profit institutions of higher education registered by the
Department provided that at least one institution offers an associate's
degree linked to the goals of the approved NYS P-TECH program, or offers
a program leading to a recognized industry certification aligned to
career readiness standards approved by the department, and which awards
the degree at no cost to the student/family; and (ii) a regional New
York State employer and/or industry/entity/association that requires
highly skilled employees which will utilize the knowledge and skills
obtained from the secondary and postsecondary programs proposed under
the application and agrees to place students who successfully complete
the program with the opportunity to be first in line for a job. School
districts that offer NYS P-TECH programs under this section shall
provide all students with disabilities and English language learners
enrolled in such program with any support services and programs required
under federal and/or State law or regulations.

Monies made available under this section can only be spent for the
following purposes: to provide additional staffing for the NYS P-TECH
program, including but not limited to a program director and college
liaison; existing evidence-based and/or standards-based curriculum that
focuses on a career in science, technology, engineering, manufacturing,
healthcare, except for the licensed professions under Title VIII of the
Education Law unless otherwise determined by the Commissioner, finance,
teaching, the arts, computer science, or math-related career area within
a NYS P-TECH program; recruitment activities for eligible students; to
provide professional development to promote the P-TECH program, includ-
ing cross-curriculum development between partners and to ensure curric-
ulum alignment that prepares students to succeed in college level cours-
es while in high school and during career training; up to ten percent of
funds awarded under this section may be used for eligible applicants to
purchase equipment needed to upgrade existing programs or new equipment
to start a program; provided that an eligible applicant may seek permis-
sion from the Commissioner for a waiver of the ten percent cap, and such
request must include a justification for why equipment in excess of the
cap is necessary to accomplish the goals of the NYS P-TECH program;
workshops and planning meetings between partners, including counselors,
parents, college faculty, and business leaders to support program
sustainability and build awareness in the regions of the benefits of
having such programs; post-secondary curriculum development that facili-
tates alignment and articulation with secondary programs leading to
college degrees and/or other industry-recognized credentials that meet
the needs of employers and provide students with increased opportunities
in life; service contracts between members of the partnership; transpor-
tation for eligible students to take courses and participate in activ-
ities at the NYS P-TECH site, at partner employers' locations, and at
the partner campus of the higher education partner; and tuition, books
and fees; provided that tuition reimbursement will only be allowable for
non-remedial, credit-bearing college courses. Monies may also be spent
to implement any corrective action plan issued under this section and/or
for tuition, books and fees for non-remedial, credit-bearing college
courses at an institution of higher education for students who were
enrolled in a NYS P-TECH program that subsequently closes before the
student completes the program; provided such student is taking compara-
ble courses to what was offered in the NYS P-TECH program as determined
by the Commissioner.

The bill further provides that no funds awarded under this section shall
be made available to support the regular academic program of any school
district or institution participating in this program.

Section 3 of the bill is the effective date.

 
STATEMENT IN SUPPORT OF THE BILL:

It is necessary to preserve and continue the NYS Smart Scholars ECHS
program and the New York State P-TECH program in this state which
provide various students, including those traditionally underrepresented
in post-secondary education, with the opportunity to access college-lev-
el courses and college degree credits at the high school level with the
combined support of high school and college staff and resources, and for
P-TECH programs, career training and employment in a highly skilled job
upon completion of the program.

The NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program not only increases access to higher
education, but also reduces potential costs for students in completing
college degrees by allowing them to either complete a degree upon gradu-
ation from high school or to apply their earned college credits towards
an Associate or Bachelor's degree. This innovative program provides
incentives to high school students to proceed to college and to earn a
college degree by accelerating their overall completion of a degree. It
also better prepares them for college-level coursework, which, will in
turn, increase their academic performance. Ultimately, this program
increases graduation rates both at the high school and college levels,
especially for academically at-risk students.

The NYS P-TECH program, through public-private partnerships, prepares
thousands of New York students for high-skill jobs of the future in
science, technology, engineering, manufacturing, healthcare, finance,
teaching, the arts, computer science, and math related career areas.
The NYS P-TECH program provides students with a rigorous, relevant and
cost-free high school and college education and a workplace learning
environment with ongoing mentoring by professionals in the chosen career
sector to better prepare these students for successful careers. Students
also receive a commitment from the participating employer to have the
opportunity to be first in line for consideration for a job following
completion of the program.

Ultimately, this program increases graduation rates both at the high
school and college levels and provides essential career training for
academically at-risk, disadvantaged students, which at the completion of
the program leads these students to a skilled job.  It is also necessary
to provide funding for these programs to ensure that they continue in
operation and continue to provide students with these valuable services.
Accelerating the completion of a student's college degree at the high
school level will result in a student requiring less financial assist-
ance (including tuition assistance or TAP funds) to complete their
degree at the post-secondary level.  These programs will ultimately
result in significant cost-savings to both the state and to families,
and, therefore, are a great investment of state funds.

It is also necessary to provide additional funding for the SED to admin-
ister and evaluate these critical programs. These funds will support
program staff to supplement the oversight and technical assistance
already being provided to these programs and ensure the timely and accu-
rate analysis of data to further enhance and validate these programs.

 
BUDGETARY IMPLICATIONS OF THE BILL:

The NYS P-TECH program and NYS Smart Scholars Early College High School
program models require intensive oversight and support, including but
not limited to: conducting training for program partners (school
districts, BOCES, institutions of higher education, and employers when
applicable) to implement the program; holding administrative training
workshops on data collection and fiscal reporting; providing ongoing
technical guidance on foundational start up responsibilities; collecting
and analyzing data; conducting site visits, particularly for new and
at-risk projects; and addressing the growing complexity of overseeing
maturing projects. Recognizing that not all students learn at the same
rate and working with historically underserved communities requires
flexibility to maximize results for students, this involves four, five
and six-year cohorts of students, each with their own needs from 9th
grade through high school graduation and up to their 2' year in college.
The cost for staff to support existing and new programs pursuant to
requests for proposals that have already been issued is estimated at
approximately $620,000.  For additional programs that are established
pursuant to a future appropriation, the Department requests a five
percent set-aside from all awards in order to allow for proper over-
sight, support, and technical assistance.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This bill was introduced in the Assembly in 2019 as A.7501 and was
referred to the Education Committee. The bill was also introduced in the
Senate in 2019 as S.6537 and passed the Senate in 2020. This bill was
introduced again in the Assembly in 2021 as A.8284 and was referred to
the Education Committee. This bill was also introduced in the Senate in
2021 as S.6825 and passed the Senate in 2022. No further action was
taken in the Assembly.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The bill would take effect immediately.
